newsitem.title: USA: Allied Healthcare refinances bank debt.
newsitem.headline: Allied Healthcare refinances bank debt.

text.p: Allied Healthcare Products Inc said Monday it has refinanced the company's existing debt through a new $46.0 million credit facility with Foothill Capital Corp, a division of Norwest Bank.

The proceeds from the new financing will be used to repay the company's outstanding debt with a previous bank group, as well as related fees and expenses, and provide additional liquidity, the company said in a news release.

The new credit facility, with a blended average interest rate of 10.2 percent, is comprised of a $25.0 million three-year revolving line of credit; two three-year term loans of $7.0 million and $10.0 million; and a $4.0 million loan maturing in six months.

In conjunction with the new financing agreement, Allied said it placed an additional $5.0 million in subordinated debt financing, with several related parties to the company; and issued warrants for 112,500 shares at an exercise price of $7.025 per share, 62,500 of which are being issued to the holders of the subordinated debt and the balance to Foothill Capital. The subordinated debt matures in six months.

"With the completion of the new financing, we can now focus our attention on improving operations and returning the company to profitability," said Uma Aggarwal, president and chief executive officer, in a statement.
Allied makes respiratory therapy equipment, medical gas equipment and emergency medical products.
